verdict.rationale: Vercel's own docs cover both halves of the story. On-demand server-side code runs on Fluid compute (Vercel Functions), and full-stack apps deploy from Git or the CLI across 40+ frameworks. Postgres and Redis integrations are explicitly provided "without managing" servers. Community reports corroborate the 'code and go' deployment experience. Limits are documented: functions have duration caps (300s default, up to 800s on Pro) and a community comment notes limited language support. missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of function deployment at depth, and a first-party statement framing Functions themselves as server-free beyond the database pages.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps with no servers to manage

citations.quote: Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
Deploy and scale web applications, APIs, and AI workloads from a Git repository or the Vercel CLI.
Deploy Next.js with zero configuration, or bring one of 40+ supported frameworks.
